claim: Perforin-2 (MPEG1) is a pore-forming, antibacterial protein with broad-spectrum activity.
source: Perforin-2 (MPEG1) is a pore-forming, antibacterial protein with broad-spectrum activity.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a characterization of Perforin-2.

claim: Perforin-2 is expressed constitutively in phagocytes.
source: Perforin-2 is expressed constitutively in phagocytes and inducibly in parenchymal, tissue-forming cells.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract.

claim: Perforin-2 is expressed inducibly in parenchymal, tissue-forming cells.
source: Perforin-2 is expressed constitutively in phagocytes and inducibly in parenchymal, tissue-forming cells.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract.

claim: In vitro, Perforin-2 prevents the intracellular replication and proliferation of bacterial pathogens in phagocytes and parenchymal cells.
source: In vitro, Perforin-2 prevents the intracellular replication and proliferation of bacterial pathogens in these cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by multiple in vitro experiments shown in the figures.

claim: Perforin-2 knockout mice are unable to control the systemic dissemination of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
source: Perforin-2 knockout mice are unable to control the systemic dissemination of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) or Salmonella typhimurium and perish shortly after epicutaneous or orogastric infection respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by in vivo infection data in Figure 7.

claim: Perforin-2 knockout mice are unable to control the systemic dissemination of Salmonella typhimurium.
source: Perforin-2 knockout mice are unable to control the systemic dissemination of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) or Salmonella typhimurium and perish shortly after epicutaneous or orogastric infection respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by in vivo infection data in Figure 8.

claim: Perforin-2 knockout mice perish shortly after epicutaneous MRSA infection.
source: Perforin-2 knockout mice are unable to control the systemic dissemination of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) or Salmonella typhimurium and perish shortly after epicutaneous or orogastric infection respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by survival curves in Figure 7A and 7B.

claim: Perforin-2 knockout mice perish shortly after orogastric Salmonella typhimurium infection.
source: Perforin-2 knockout mice are unable to control the systemic dissemination of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) or Salmonella typhimurium and perish shortly after epicutaneous or orogastric infection respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by survival curves in Figure 8A and 8B.

claim: Perforin-2-sufficient littermates clear MRSA and Salmonella typhimurium infections.
source: In contrast, Perforin-2-sufficient littermates clear the infection.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by survival and CFU data in Figures 7 and 8.

claim: Perforin-2 is a transmembrane protein of cytosolic vesicles derived from multiple organelles.
source: Perforin-2 is a transmembrane protein of cytosolic vesicles -derived from multiple organelles- that translocate to and fuse with bacterium containing vesicles.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by fractionation and imaging data in Figure 4.

claim: Perforin-2-containing vesicles translocate to and fuse with bacterium containing vesicles.
source: Perforin-2 is a transmembrane protein of cytosolic vesicles -derived from multiple organelles- that translocate to and fuse with bacterium containing vesicles.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by confocal imaging in Figure 4D-I.

claim: Perforin-2 polymerizes and forms large clusters of 100 Å pores in the bacterial surface.
source: Subsequently, Perforin-2 polymerizes and forms large clusters of 100 Å pores in the bacterial surface with Perforin-2 cleavage products present in bacteria.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by electron microscopy data in Figure 5.

claim: Perforin-2 cleavage products are present in bacteria.
source: Subsequently, Perforin-2 polymerizes and forms large clusters of 100 Å pores in the bacterial surface with Perforin-2 cleavage products present in bacteria.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by Western blot data in Figure 6.

claim: Perforin-2 is required for the bactericidal activity of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species.
source: Perforin-2 is also required for the bactericidal activity of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species and hydrolytic enzymes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by inhibitor experiments in Figure 2.

claim: Perforin-2 is required for the bactericidal activity of hydrolytic enzymes.
source: Perforin-2 is also required for the bactericidal activity of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species and hydrolytic enzymes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract.

claim: Perforin-2 constitutes a novel and apparently essential bactericidal effector molecule of the innate immune system.
source: Perforin-2 constitutes a novel and apparently essential bactericidal effector molecule of the innate immune system.
evidence: This is the concluding statement of the abstract, summarizing the overall findings.

claim: C9 polymerizes and forms 100 Å pores in bacterial surfaces.
source: This finding resolved the question of the molecular nature of the membrane attack complex of complement (MAC) (Humphrey and Dourmashkin, 1969; Mayer, 1972; Muller-Eberhard, 1975; Bhakdi and Tranum-Jensen, 1978) where C5b-8 complexes, first assembled around membrane-bound C3b, trigger C9 to polymerize and form 100 Å pores in bacterial surfaces (Schreiber et al., 1979; Podack and Tschopp, 1982; Tschopp et al., 1982).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Perforin-1 was identified as the pore-forming killer protein for virus-infected cells and tumor cells.
source: Analysis of natural killer (NK) cells and cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTL) identified Perforin-1 as the pore-forming killer protein for virus-infected cells and tumor cells (Dennert and Podack, 1983; Podack and Dennert, 1983; Blumenthal et al., 1984).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Sequence alignment of Perforin-1 and C9 identified a conserved domain named the Membrane Attack Complex/Perforin (MACPF) domain.
source: Sequence alignment of Perforin-1 and C9 identified a conserved domain, named the Membrane Attack Complex/Perforin (MACPF) domain in reference to its founding members (Lichtenheld et al., 1988).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: During polymerization, the MACPF-domains of individual protomers refold and expose an amphipathic helix that inserts into the targeted membranes.
source: During polymerization, the MACPF-domains of individual protomers refold and expose an amphipathic helix that inserts into the targeted membranes (Rosado et al., 2007; Baran et al., 2009; Kondos et al., 2010; Law et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: MACPF generated pores disrupt the innate barrier function of membranes and provide access for chemical or enzymatic effectors.
source: MACPF generated pores disrupt the innate barrier function of membranes and provide access for chemical or enzymatic effectors that finalize destruction of the target (Schreiber et al., 1979; Masson and Tschopp, 1987; Trapani et al., 1988; Shiver et al., 1992; Smyth et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Macrophage Expressed Gene 1 (MPEG1) is the most recently identified protein with a MACPF-domain.
source: Macrophage Expressed Gene 1 (MPEG1) is the most recently identified protein with a MACPF-domain (Spilsbury et al., 1995).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: MPEG1 was renamed Perforin-2 when it was confirmed to be a pore forming protein.
source: We renamed the new MACPF-containing protein Perforin-2 when we confirmed that it also was a pore forming protein.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction.

claim: Perforin-2 is one of the oldest eukaryotic MACPF members, present in early metazoan phyla including Porifera (sponges).
source: Evolutionary studies of Perforin-2, have demonstrated that Perforin-2 is one of the oldest eukaryotic MACPF members, present in early metazoan phyla including Porifera (sponges) (D'Angelo et al., 2012; Wiens et al., 2005; McCormack et al., 2013a; McCormack et al., 2013b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Orthologues of Perforin-2 are highly conserved throughout the animal kingdom.
source: Orthologues of Perforin-2 are highly conserved throughout the animal kingdom (Mah et al., 2004; Wiens et al., 2005; Wang et al., 2008; He et al., 2011; Kemp and Coyne, 2011; Green et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Expression of Perforin-2 is not limited to macrophages, as it was also detected in murine embryonic fibroblasts (MEF) and human epithelial cells after bacterial infection.
source: Recent studies in vertebrates (mammalia) demonstrate that expression of Perforin-2 is not limited to macrophages, as it was also detected in murine embryonic fibroblasts (MEF) and human epithelial cells after bacterial infection (Fields et al., 2013; McCormack et al., 2013a) suggesting that Perforin-2 expression is tied to antibacterial activity.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In Zebrafish, one of its two Perforin-2 isoforms, MPEG1.2, is induced following bacterial infection and limits bacterial burden.
source: Similarly, in Zebrafish one of its two isoforms, MPEG1.2, is induced following bacterial infection and limits bacterial burden (Benard et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Perforin-2-deficient murine peritoneal exudate macrophages (PEM) are unable to kill Mycobacterium smegmatis.
source: Perforin-2-deficient murine peritoneal exudate macrophages (PEM), neutrophils, and bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDM) are unable to kill three different species of Mycobacteria (Mycobacterium smegmatis, Mycobacterium avium, M. tuberculosis), as indicated by significant intracellular bacterial replication in MPEG1 (Perforin-2) −/− compared to +/+ or +/− phagocytes (Figure 1A–C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 1A.

claim: Perforin-2-deficient murine neutrophils are unable to kill Mycobacterium avium.
source: Perforin-2-deficient murine peritoneal exudate macrophages (PEM), neutrophils, and bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDM) are unable to kill three different species of Mycobacteria (Mycobacterium smegmatis, Mycobacterium avium, M. tuberculosis), as indicated by significant intracellular bacterial replication in MPEG1 (Perforin-2) −/− compared to +/+ or +/− phagocytes (Figure 1A–C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 1B.

claim: Perforin-2-deficient murine bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDM) are unable to kill M. tuberculosis.
source: Perforin-2-deficient murine peritoneal exudate macrophages (PEM), neutrophils, and bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDM) are unable to kill three different species of Mycobacteria (Mycobacterium smegmatis, Mycobacterium avium, M. tuberculosis), as indicated by significant intracellular bacterial replication in MPEG1 (Perforin-2) −/− compared to +/+ or +/− phagocytes (Figure 1A–C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 1C.

claim: BMDM must be activated with IFN and LPS in order to mediate Perforin-2-dependent growth inhibition of M. tuberculosis.
source: Although BMDM express Perforin-2 constitutively, they must be activated with IFN and LPS in order to mediate Perforin-2-dependent growth inhibition of M. tuberculosis (Mtb) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Perforin-2 knockdown in BV2 microglia cells can be complemented by Perforin-2-RFP.
source: To exclude the possibility of off-target protein effects by Perforin-2-siRNA, we performed complementation assays in BV2-microglia with C-terminally tagged Perforin-2-RFP (Figure 1D–G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 1D-G.

claim: Only Perforin-2-RFP but not control RFP transfection restored bactericidal activity in Perforin-2 knockdown cells.
source: Only Perforin-2-RFP but not control RFP transfection restored bactericidal activity.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 1D-G.

claim: Human macrophages and neutrophils express Perforin-2 protein constitutively.
source: Human macrophages and neutrophils express Perforin-2 protein constitutively (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Human monocyte derived macrophages (MDM) efficiently killed intracellular MRSA.
source: Human monocyte derived macrophages (MDM) efficiently killed intracellular MRSA.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 1I.

claim: Perforin-2 knockdown by siRNA abrogated killing of MRSA and resulted in MRSA replication in human MDM.
source: Perforin-2 knockdown by siRNA abrogated killing of MRSA and resulted in MRSA replication (Figure 1 I).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 1I.

claim: Perforin-2 siRNA silencing in RA-differentiated HL-60 cells abolished Perforin-2 protein expression.
source: Perforin-2 siRNA silencing in RA-differentiated HL-60 cells abolished Perforin-2 protein expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 3) and was associated with intracellular replication of Salmonella typhimurium, MRSA, and M. smegmatis (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Perforin-2 siRNA silencing in RA-differentiated HL-60 cells was associated with intracellular replication of Salmonella typhimurium, MRSA, and M. smegmatis.
source: Perforin-2 siRNA silencing in RA-differentiated HL-60 cells abolished Perforin-2 protein expression (Figure 1—figure supplement 3) and was associated with intracellular replication of Salmonella typhimurium, MRSA, and M. smegmatis (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Professional murine and human phagocytes require Perforin-2 to kill phagocytosed bacteria.
source: In summary, the results indicate that professional murine and human phagocytes require Perforin-2 to kill phagocytosed bacteria.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the data presented in Figure 1 and its supplements.

claim: PEM activated by IFN-γ and LPS produce both ROS and RNS.
source: PEM activated by IFN-γ and LPS produce both families of effectors (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: In Perforin-2 deficient PEM, S. typhimurium replicated equally well regardless of ROS inhibition.
source: In Perforin-2 deficient PEM, S. typhimurium replicated equally well regardless of ROS inhibition (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2B.

claim: ROS had minimal influence on intracellular replication of S. typhimurium in the absence of Perforin-2.
source: This suggests ROS had minimal influence on intracellular replication of S. typhimurium in the absence of Perforin-2.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data in Figure 2B.

claim: In PEM that express Perforin-2, the inhibition of endogenous ROS by NAC enables S. typhimurium to replicate significantly more than mock treatment during the first 4 hr after infection.
source: In contrast, with PEM that express Perforin-2, the inhibition of endogenous ROS by NAC enables S. typhimurium to replicate significantly more than mock treatment during the first 4 hr after infection, suggesting that ROS in combination with Perforin-2 helps to restrain S. typhimurium replication during this period (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2A.

claim: ROS in combination with Perforin-2 helps to restrain S. typhimurium replication during the first 4 hr after infection.
source: In contrast, with PEM that express Perforin-2, the inhibition of endogenous ROS by NAC enables S. typhimurium to replicate significantly more than mock treatment during the first 4 hr after infection, suggesting that ROS in combination with Perforin-2 helps to restrain S. typhimurium replication during this period (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data in Figure 2A.

claim: Inhibition of endogenous NO production with L-NAME in the presence of Perforin-2 allowed increased intracellular S. typhimurium replication beginning several hours post-infection.
source: Inhibition of endogenous NO production with L-NAME in the presence of Perforin-2 also allowed increased intracellular S. typhimurium replication beginning several hours post-infection (Figure 2C) coinciding with the known time period required for onset of NO production (see Figure 2—figure supplement 1) (Mastroeni et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2C.

claim: Endogenous NO had little effect on S. typhimurium replication in the absence of Perforin-2.
source: As with ROS, endogenous NO had little effect on S. typhimurium replication in the absence of Perforin-2 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2D.

claim: Although ROS and NO contribute towards the intracellular killing of bacterial pathogens, their bactericidal activity is largely dependent upon the presence of Perforin-2.
source: The results indicate that although ROS and NO contribute towards the intracellular killing of bacterial pathogens, their bactericidal activity is largely dependent upon the presence of Perforin-2.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the data presented in Figure 2.

claim: The cooperative activity of Perforin-2 with ROS and NO was also evident in killing of M. smegmatis in PEM.
source: The cooperative activity of Perforin-2 with ROS and NO was also evident in killing of M. smegmatis in PEM (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Pharmacologic inhibitors significantly increased bacterial survival only when Perforin-2 was present, with little additional effect when Perforin-2 was absent.
source: Pharmacologic inhibitors significantly increased bacterial survival only when Perforin-2 was present, with little additional effect when Perforin-2 was absent.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The critical importance of Perforin-2 in facilitating ROS and NO activity is not specific to only S. typhimurium.
source: This data suggested that the critical importance of Perforin-2 in facilitating ROS and NO activity is not specific to only S. typhimurium.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the data with M. smegmatis in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: In the presence of Perforin-2, SodC1-deficient S. typhimurium were killed more efficiently than wild-type S. typhimurium.
source: In the presence of Perforin-2, SodC1-deficient S. typhimurium were killed more efficiently than wild-type S. typhimurium.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2E.

claim: SodC1-deficient S. typhimurium replicate similar to wild-type S. typhimurium when Perforin-2 was absent.
source: However, SodC1-deficient S. typhimurium replicate similar to wild-type S. typhimurium when Perforin-2 was absent (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2E.

claim: hmpA mutants are more susceptible to killing by NO than wild-type bacteria, but only when Perforin-2 is present.
source: Similarly, hmpA mutants are more susceptible to killing by NO than wild-type bacteria, but only when Perforin-2 is present.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2F.

claim: In the absence of Perforin-2, Flavohemoglobin does not enhance the survival and replication of wild-type S. typhimurium relative to the hmpA mutant.
source: In the absence of Perforin-2, Flavohemoglobin does not enhance the survival and replication of wild-type S. typhimurium relative to the hmpA mutant.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2F.

claim: Both chemical and genetic analyses indicate that Perforin-2 is required for the bactericidal activity of ROS and NO in macrophages.
source: Thus, both chemical and genetic analyses indicate that Perforin-2 is required for the bactericidal activity of ROS and NO in macrophages.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the data presented in Figure 2.

claim: Every cell type derived from ectodermal, neuroectodermal, endodermal, or mesodermal lineage tested to date is able to express Perforin-2 message either constitutively or after type I or II IFN induction.
source: Every cell type derived from ectodermal, neuroectodermal, endodermal, or mesodermal lineage tested to date is able to express Perforin-2 message either constitutively or after type I or II IFN induction.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Tables 1 and 2.

claim: All cell types analyzed (54 out of 54) are able to kill bacteria in an in vitro bactericidal assay when Perforin-2 is expressed.
source: Moreover, all cell types analyzed (54 out of 54) are able to kill bacteria in an in vitro bactericidal assay when Perforin-2 is expressed.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Tables 1 and 2 and Supplementary files 1-4.

claim: When infection occurs prior to Perforin-2 induction or when Perforin-2 is siRNA-ablated or genetically deficient, bacteria were not killed by cells and consequently replicate.
source: When infection occurs prior to Perforin-2 induction or when Perforin-2 is siRNA-ablated or genetically deficient using the above assay, bacteria were not killed by cells and consequently replicate.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 3 and its supplements.

claim: Cells that express Perforin-2 were bactericidal.
source: In contrast, cells that express Perforin-2 were bactericidal.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 3 and its supplements.

claim: Perforin-2 can be expressed ubiquitously to defend cells against bacterial invasion.
source: These results suggest that Perforin-2 can be expressed ubiquitously to defend cells against bacterial invasion.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the data in Tables 1 and 2 and Figure 3.

claim: After overnight induction with IFN-γ, MPEG1 (Perforin-2) +/+ MEFs eliminate MRSA.
source: After overnight induction with IFN-γ, MPEG1 (Perforin-2) +/+ MEFs eliminate MRSA.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 3D.

claim: IFN-γ treated Perforin-2 −/− MEFs enable MRSA to replicate.
source: In contrast, IFN-γ treated Perforin-2 −/− MEFs enable MRSA to replicate.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 3D.

claim: Heterozygous MEFs had intermediate bactericidal activity suggesting a gene dose effect of Perforin-2.
source: Heterozygous MEFs had intermediate bactericidal activity (Figure 3D) suggesting a gene dose effect of Perforin-2.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 3D.

claim: Primary human keratinocytes express Perforin-2 constitutively.
source: Unlike other parenchymal cells that need to be induced, primary human Kc express Perforin-2 constitutively.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The inhibition of Perforin-2 expression abrogated the bactericidal activity of keratinocytes.
source: The inhibition of Perforin-2 expression abrogated the bactericidal activity of Kc (Figure 3E) that were able to kill MRSA, irrespective of prior IFN activation (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 3E.

claim: Keratinocytes were able to kill MRSA, irrespective of prior IFN activation.
source: The inhibition of Perforin-2 expression abrogated the bactericidal activity of Kc (Figure 3E) that were able to kill MRSA, irrespective of prior IFN activation (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 3F.

claim: Perforin-2 is an effector for cellular defense against pathogenic bacteria in professional phagocytes and in other cells.
source: Cumulatively, our results suggest that Perforin-2 is an effector for cellular defense against pathogenic bacteria in professional phagocytes and in other cells.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the data presented in Figures 1-3.

claim: The ubiquity of Perforin-2 expression suggests a critical importance in cellular defenses of many, if not all, tissue against pathogenic bacteria.
source: The ubiquity of Perforin-2 expression suggests a critical importance in cellular defenses of many, if not all, tissue against pathogenic bacteria.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the data in Tables 1 and 2.

claim: In non-infected murine BV2 microglial cells, Perforin-2-GFP vesicles were distributed in a membrane pattern throughout the cell.
source: In non-infected murine BV2 microglial cells, Perforin-2-GFP vesicles were distributed in a membrane pattern throughout the cell (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by confocal imaging in Figure 4C.

claim: Following S. typhimurium infection, Perforin-2-GFP redistributed and accumulated, within minutes, on endosomal/phagosomal bodies.
source: Following S. typhimurium infection, Perforin-2-GFP redistributed and accumulated, within minutes, on endosomal/phagosomal bodies (Figure 4D–F, red arrows) that contained diffuse DNA as indicated by DAPI staining of phagocytosed S. typhimurium as compared to an intact extracellular S. typhimurium bacillus with its typical rod-like morphology (white arrow).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by confocal imaging in Figure 4D-F.

claim: Perforin-2-RFP is largely concentrated on phagosomes that contain E. coli-GFP.
source: Fluorescent imaging indicated that Perforin-2-RFP is largely concentrated on phagosomes that contain E. coli-GFP (Figure 4G–I).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by confocal imaging in Figure 4G-I.

claim: Perforin-2 is able to rapidly translocate to endosomal membranes, or in some cells may already be localized in these membranes in order to trap intracellular bacteria.
source: Overall, these studies demonstrated that Perforin-2 is able to rapidly translocate to endosomal membranes, or in some cells may already be localized in these membranes in order to trap intracellular bacteria (upon fusion with phagosomes).
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the data presented in Figure 4.

claim: Clusters of typical membrane pores of ∼100 Å inner diameter were observed in membranes from Perforin-2 overexpressing HEK-293 cells after trypsin treatment.
source: We observed clusters of typical membrane pores of ∼100 Å inner diameter in these membranes (Figure 5A,B) that were morphologically similar to poly-C9 and poly-Perforin-1 pores on bacterial and cell membranes (Schreiber et al., 1979; Podack and Tschopp, 1982; Podack and Dennert, 1983).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by electron microscopy data in Figure 5A,B.

claim: Pores were not observed on any membranes in the absence of trypsin treatment.
source: Pores were not observed on any membranes in the absence of trypsin treatment.
evidence: This is stated in the text.

claim: Perforin-2, putatively via its MACPF domain, is able to form clusters of regular polymeric pores on membranes akin to C9 of complement and Perforin-1.
source: These experiments suggest that Perforin-2, putatively via its MACPF domain, is able to form clusters of regular polymeric pores on membranes akin to C9 of complement and Perforin-1.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the electron microscopy data in Figure 5A,B.

claim: Large patches of densely clustered pores of ca. 100 Å inner diameter are visualized on both MRSA and M. smegmatis surfaces isolated from Perforin-2 expressing MEFs.
source: Large patches of densely clustered pores of ca. 100 Å inner diameter are visualized on both MRSA and M. smegmatis surfaces with similar irregularities as those observed in complement lesions on E. coli surfaces (Schreiber et al., 1979).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by electron microscopy data in Figure 5C-G.

claim: Pores are only visible after bacteria were isolated from cells expressing Perforin-2.
source: Pores are only visible after bacteria were isolated from cells expressing Perforin-2.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by blinded quantification in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Pores were not present on control bacteria or after isolation of bacteria from Perforin-2 deficient cells as determined by blinded quantification of the pore-like structures.
source: Pores were not present on control bacteria or after isolation of bacteria from Perforin-2 deficient cells as determined by blinded quantification of the pore-like structures (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: There were significantly greater numbers of pore-like structures (two or more orders of magnitude) associated with bacteria isolated from Perforin-2 expressing cells compared to Perforin-2 deficient cells.
source: There were significantly greater numbers of pore-like structures (two or more orders of magnitude) associated with bacteria isolated from Perforin-2 expressing cells compared to Perforin-2 deficient cells.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: There is a strong correlation between pore-formation and Perforin-2.
source: This indicates that there is a strong correlation between pore-formation and Perforin-2.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Perforin-2 reactive bands with different molecular weights were detected in fractions containing either EPEC or MRSA.
source: Following the isolation procedure and subsequent differential rounds of centrifugation, Perforin-2 reactive bands with different molecular weights were detected in fractions containing either EPEC or MRSA.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in Figure 6.

claim: Perforin-2 was not detected after bacterial fractions were passed through 0.22 μM filters.
source: Perforin-2 was not detected after these fractions were passed through 0.22 μM filters (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in Figure 6.

claim: Perforin-2 was not present as a soluble protein nor associated with cellular debris or microvesicles.
source: This indicates that Perforin-2 was not present as a soluble protein nor associated with cellular debris or microvesicles.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the filtration data in Figure 6.

claim: Perforin-2 was associated with particles larger than 0.22 microns, such as bacterial cells.
source: Rather, Perforin-2 was associated with particles larger than 0.22 microns, such as bacterial cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the filtration data in Figure 6.

claim: Antibodies directed to the amino-terminal domains detected Perforin-2 in bacterial fractions.
source: Antibodies directed to the amino-terminal domains detected Perforin-2 in bacterial fractions.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in Figure 6.

claim: A single ca. 50 kD band was detected after probing with an antibody targeting amino-terminal portion of the Perforin-2 domain.
source: A single ca. 50 kD band was detected after probing with an antibody targeting amino-terminal portion of the Perforin-2 domain.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in Figure 6.

claim: Probing with either carboxy- or amino-terminal MACPF domain antibodies recognized two bands in the bacterial fractions.
source: Probing with either carboxy- or amino-terminal MACPF domain antibodies recognized two bands in the bacterial fractions.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in Figure 6.

claim: One band detected by MACPF domain antibodies is the same size as the ca. 50kD band observed with the amino-terminal detecting Perforin-2 domain antibody, suggesting that this band is a combination of the MACPF domain and an amino-terminal portion of the Perforin-2 domain.
source: One of these bands is the same size as the ca. 50kD band observed with the amino-terminal detecting Perforin-2 domain antibody, suggesting that this band is a combination of the MACPF domain and an amino-terminal portion of the Perforin-2 domain.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the Western blot data in Figure 6.

claim: Both MACPF domain antibodies also identified another band of ca. 37kD that is not detected with the Perforin-2 domain antibody, indicative of a MACPF domain fragment.
source: Both MACPF domain antibodies also identified another band of ca. 37kD that is not detected with the Perforin-2 domain antibody, indicative of a MACPF domain fragment.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Western blot data in Figure 6.

claim: Antibodies raised against the carboxy-terminal region of the Perforin-2 domain, the cytoplasmic domain, or the GFP tag were negative in unfiltered bacterial fractions.
source: Antibodies raised against the carboxy-terminal region of the Perforin-2 domain, the cytoplasmic domain, or the GFP tag were negative in unfiltered bacterial fractions despite validation of both Perforin-2 peptide antibodies with human macrophage whole cell lysates (data not shown, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text.

claim: These results indicate that Perforin-2 makes physical contact with bacteria.
source: These results indicate that Perforin-2 makes physical contact with bacteria are supports are interpretation of electron dense poly-Perforin-2 pores.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the Western blot data in Figure 6.

claim: Perforin-2 was neither vital for developmental processes nor for the control of commensal bacteria under specific pathogen-free conditions.
source: Perforin-2 was neither vital for developmental processes nor for the control of commensal bacteria under specific pathogen-free conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the text.

claim: Perforin-2 was not vital for the regular development of the innate and adaptive immune system.
source: This specifically included the regular development of the innate and adaptive immune system (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Perforin-2 knockout mice exhibited significantly decreased survival compared to Perforin-2 heterozygous or wild-type littermates after epicutaneous MRSA challenge.
source: Perforin-2 knockout mice exhibited significantly decreased survival and more weight loss compared to Perforin-2 heterozygous or wild-type littermates (Figure 7A,B, Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by survival curves in Figure 7A,B.

claim: Perforin-2 knockout mice exhibited more weight loss compared to Perforin-2 heterozygous or wild-type littermates after epicutaneous MRSA challenge.
source: Perforin-2 knockout mice exhibited significantly decreased survival and more weight loss compared to Perforin-2 heterozygous or wild-type littermates (Figure 7A,B, Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by weight loss data in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: On day 6 after MRSA infection, all groups showed signs of systemic MRSA infection.
source: On day 6, all groups showed signs of systemic MRSA infection (recoverable CFU from internal organs).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CFU data in Figure 7—figure supplement 3.

claim: CFUs in Perforin-2 −/− mice were significantly higher than in wild-type mice on day 6 after MRSA infection.
source: However, CFUs in Perforin-2 −/− mice were significantly higher than in wild-type mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 3) and by day 12, Perforin-2 deficient mice continued to have bacteremia with 100 to 100,000 fold higher MRSA counts in their organs as compared to Perforin-2 heterozygous or wild-type littermates (Figure 7B–E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CFU data in Figure 7—figure supplement 3.

claim: By day 12 after MRSA infection, Perforin-2 deficient mice continued to have bacteremia with 100 to 100,000 fold higher MRSA counts in their organs as compared to Perforin-2 heterozygous or wild-type littermates.
source: However, CFUs in Perforin-2 −/− mice were significantly higher than in wild-type mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 3) and by day 12, Perforin-2 deficient mice continued to have bacteremia with 100 to 100,000 fold higher MRSA counts in their organs as compared to Perforin-2 heterozygous or wild-type littermates (Figure 7B–E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CFU data in Figure 7C-F.

claim: The majority of heterozygous animals completely cleared the MRSA infection by day 12.
source: The majority of heterozygous animals completely cleared the infection, with only a few mice demonstrating recoverable CFU in internal organs and the skin at day 12 (Figure 7B–E) while MRSA of the wild-type animals could only be recovered from the skin of three animals.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CFU data in Figure 7C-F.

claim: MRSA of the wild-type animals could only be recovered from the skin of three animals at day 12.
source: The majority of heterozygous animals completely cleared the infection, with only a few mice demonstrating recoverable CFU in internal organs and the skin at day 12 (Figure 7B–E) while MRSA of the wild-type animals could only be recovered from the skin of three animals.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CFU data in Figure 7C-F.

claim: All Perforin-2 knockout mice failed to eliminate MRSA and recover their weight.
source: On the other hand, all Perforin-2 knockout mice failed to eliminate MRSA and recover their weight.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by survival and weight loss data in Figure 7A,B and Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: All Perforin-2 knockout mice eventually succumbed to MRSA infection.
source: These animals eventually succumbed to infection (Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by survival curves in Figure 7A,B.

claim: Similar trends in MRSA mortality were observed with 129X1/SVJ congenic animals.
source: Similar trends were observed with 129X1/SVJ congenic animals (Figure 7B) indicating that MRSA mortality was controlled by Perforin-2 and not attributable to confounding passenger mutations or genetic background differences between 129X1/SVJ and C57Bl/6 mice (Vanden Berghe et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by survival curves in Figure 7B.

claim: MRSA mortality was controlled by Perforin-2 and not attributable to confounding passenger mutations or genetic background differences between 129X1/SVJ and C57Bl/6 mice.
source: Similar trends were observed with 129X1/SVJ congenic animals (Figure 7B) indicating that MRSA mortality was controlled by Perforin-2 and not attributable to confounding passenger mutations or genetic background differences between 129X1/SVJ and C57Bl/6 mice (Vanden Berghe et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the data in Figure 7B and supported by a citation.

claim: MRSA replicated in Perforin-2 −/− neutrophils, but was killed in the presence of Perforin-2.
source: We found that MRSA replicated in Perforin-2 −/− neutrophils, but was killed in the presence of Perforin-2.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 7G.

claim: Heterozygous neutrophils had intermediate bactericidal activity towards MRSA, suggesting that Perforin-2 was a rate-limiting molecule to control intracellular MRSA after infection.
source: Heterozygous neutrophils had intermediate bactericidal activity towards MRSA, suggesting that Perforin-2 was a rate-limiting molecule to control intracellular MRSA after infection (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 7G.

claim: Perforin-2 is required to limit the early systemic dissemination of MRSA.
source: These in vivo results indicate that Perforin-2 is required to limit the early systemic dissemination of MRSA (Hahn et al., 2009; Onunkwo et al., 2010) and, ultimately, to clear epicutaneous MRSA infection.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the in vivo data in Figure 7 and supported by citations.

claim: Perforin-2 is required to clear epicutaneous MRSA infection.
source: These in vivo results indicate that Perforin-2 is required to limit the early systemic dissemination of MRSA (Hahn et al., 2009; Onunkwo et al., 2010) and, ultimately, to clear epicutaneous MRSA infection.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the in vivo data in Figure 7.

claim: Perforin-2 wild-type animals only transiently lost weight (<10%) after orogastric S. typhimurium infection with 10^5 CFU.
source: As expected for this low infectious inoculum, Perforin-2 wild-type animals only transiently lost weight (<10%) whereas Perforin-2 deficient mice progressively lost weight and acquired severe diarrhea.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by weight loss data in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Perforin-2 deficient mice progressively lost weight and acquired severe diarrhea after orogastric S. typhimurium infection with 10^5 CFU.
source: As expected for this low infectious inoculum, Perforin-2 wild-type animals only transiently lost weight (<10%) whereas Perforin-2 deficient mice progressively lost weight and acquired severe diarrhea.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by weight loss data in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Perforin-2 heterozygous littermates had more severe initial weight loss than wild-type animals after orogastric S. typhimurium infection, but these animals were able to recover.
source: Perforin-2 heterozygous littermates had more severe initial weight loss than wild-type animals, but these animals were able to recover (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by weight loss data in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: Equal S. typhimurium inoculation and colonization was confirmed by CFU analysis of the feces 12 hr following S. typhimurium inoculation.
source: Equal S. typhimurium inoculation and colonization was confirmed by CFU analysis of the feces 12 hr following S. typhimurium inoculation (Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CFU data in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: The observed Perforin-2 phenotype in S. typhimurium infection did not result from genetic differences because the aggregated survival curves were similar in 129X1/SVJ congenic animals.
source: As with the MRSA experiments, the observed Perforin-2 phenotype did not result from genetic differences because the aggregated survival curves were similar (compare Figure 8B with Figure 8A).
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the survival curves in Figure 8A and 8B.

claim: At 60 hr following S. typhimurium infection, all three Perforin-2 groups showed signs of systemic S. typhimurium infection.
source: At this time point all three Perforin-2 groups showed signs of systemic S. typhimurium infection; however, with CFUs in Perforin-2 −/− mice were significantly higher than in wild-type animals.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CFU data in Figure 8—figure supplement 3.

claim: At 60 hr following S. typhimurium infection, CFUs in Perforin-2 −/− mice were significantly higher than in wild-type animals.
source: At this time point all three Perforin-2 groups showed signs of systemic S. typhimurium infection; however, with CFUs in Perforin-2 −/− mice were significantly higher than in wild-type animals.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CFU data in Figure 8—figure supplement 3.

claim: Only Perforin-2 −/− animals were septic with high bacterial titers in the blood at 60 hr following S. typhimurium infection.
source: Moreover, only the former animals were septic with high bacterial titers in the blood.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CFU data in Figure 8—figure supplement 3A.

claim: 5 days following S. typhimurium infection, the bacterial burden of S. typhimurium in Perforin-2 −/− mice continued to be significantly higher in all organs as compared to their MPEG1 (Perforin-2) +/+ littermates.
source: 5 days following infection, the bacterial burden of S. typhimurium in Perforin-2 −/− mice continued to be significantly higher in all organs as compared to their MPEG1 (Perforin-2) +/+ littermates (Figure 8C–F) with intermediate levels observed in the heterozygous littermates.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CFU data in Figure 8C-F.

claim: Intermediate levels of S. typhimurium were observed in the heterozygous littermates at 5 days following infection.
source: 5 days following infection, the bacterial burden of S. typhimurium in Perforin-2 −/− mice continued to be significantly higher in all organs as compared to their MPEG1 (Perforin-2) +/+ littermates (Figure 8C–F) with intermediate levels observed in the heterozygous littermates.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by CFU data in Figure 8C-F.

claim: Perforin-2 is required to clear S. typhimurium.
source: These in vivo results indicate that Perforin-2 is also required to clear S. typhimurium, and other compensatory bactericidal mechanisms are unable to contain orogastric S. typhimurium contributing to the rapid systemic spread of the pathogen.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the in vivo data in Figure 8.

claim: Other compensatory bactericidal mechanisms are unable to contain orogastric S. typhimurium contributing to the rapid systemic spread of the pathogen in the absence of Perforin-2.
source: These in vivo results indicate that Perforin-2 is also required to clear S. typhimurium, and other compensatory bactericidal mechanisms are unable to contain orogastric S. typhimurium contributing to the rapid systemic spread of the pathogen.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the in vivo data in Figure 8.

claim: In the absence of Perforin-2, the ability of phagocytes and parenchymal cells to destroy bacteria is severely compromised.
source: In this study we have characterized an additional effector, Perforin-2, present in professional phagocytes and barrier forming cells such as keratinocytes and mucosal epithelial cells. In the absence of Perforin-2, the ability of these cells to destroy bacteria is severely compromised (Figure 2, Table 1, Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Perforin-2 may act upstream of other antimicrobial effectors or that their potency is enhanced by Perforin-2.
source: These findings suggest that Perforin-2 may act upstream of other antimicrobial effectors or that their potency is enhanced by Perforin-2.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation stated in the discussion.

claim: Parenchymal, tissue-forming cells can express Perforin-2 and its expression in these cells is essential for killing of bacteria.
source: Our study demonstrates that parenchymal, tissue-forming cells can also express Perforin-2 and its expression in these cells is essential for killing of bacteria.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figure 3 and Tables 1 and 2.

claim: EM analysis of isolated bacteria suggests that bacterial killing is achieved by polymerization and pore-formation of Perforin-2.
source: Our EM analysis of isolated bacteria suggests that this killing is achieved by polymerization and pore-formation of Perforin-2.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by electron microscopy data in Figure 5.

claim: In the absence of Perforin-2, the other innate defense effectors were unable to prevent the replication and systemic dissemination of bacterial pathogens.
source: In the absence of Perforin-2, the other innate defense effectors were unable to prevent the replication and systemic dissemination of bacterial pathogens.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by in vivo data in Figures 7 and 8.

claim: Perforin-2 may facilitate or augment the activity of other antimicrobial effectors.
source: As per above, this suggests that Perforin-2 may facilitate or augment the activity of other antimicrobial effectors.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation stated in the discussion.

claim: The unique structure of Perforin-2 as a membrane protein with a luminal and extracellular MACPF-killer domain is well suited for locally killing membrane-entrapped, extracellular or intracellular bacteria.
source: The unique structure of Perforin-2 as a membrane protein with a luminal and extracellular MACPF-killer domain is well suited for locally killing membrane-entrapped, extracellular or intracellular bacteria.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation stated in the discussion.

claim: Seemingly every cell can utilize Perforin-2 to defend itself against bacteria—potentially even before professional phagocytes are recruited.
source: Seemingly every cell can utilize Perforin-2 to defend itself against bacteria—potentially even before professional phagocytes are recruited–according to the constitutive expression of Perforin-2 in kc.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation stated in the discussion.

claim: The lack of barrier protection by keratinocytes when Perforin-2 is deficient may explain why Perforin-2 knockout mice rapidly exhibit symptoms to epicutaneous infection with MRSA.
source: Owing to this innate intrinsic protection of kc, bacteria may be cleared by these barrier cells even before the influx and assistance of professional phagocytes. The lack of barrier protection by kc when Perforin-2 is deficient may explain why Perforin-2 knockout mice rapidly (within days; Figure 7—figure supplement 2) exhibit symptoms to epicutaneous infection with MRSA.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation stated in the discussion.

claim: The combined absence of Perforin-2 in the barrier tissue and in professional phagocytes may overwhelm the host by enhancing the systemic dissemination of the bacteria.
source: Thereafter the combined absence of Perforin-2 in the barrier tissue and in professional phagocytes may overwhelm the host by enhancing the systemic dissemination of the bacteria (Figure 7—figure supplement 3) and, ultimately, leading to multiple organ failure.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation stated in the discussion.

claim: The speed and severity of infections in Perforin-2 deficient animals, including sepsis and death following traditional non-lethal inocula of bacteria, may be assisted by the seemingly ubiquitous expression and function of Perforin-2.
source: The speed and severity of infections in Perforin-2 deficient animals, including sepsis and death following traditional non-lethal inocula of bacteria (Figures 7, 8), may also be assisted by the seemingly ubiquitous expression and function of Perforin-2, either inducible or constitutive.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation stated in the discussion.

claim: Ubiquitous Perforin-2 expression provides heretofore unrealized defenses at all potential sites of infection including barrier cells, phagocytes, parenchyma, and possibly even stroma.
source: We suggest that this ubiquitous mechanism provides heretofore unrealized defenses at all potential sites of infection including barrier cells, phagocytes, parenchyma, and possibly even stroma.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation stated in the discussion.

claim: Unactivated parenchymal cells offer invasive bacteria a window of opportunity for replication and further dissemination.
source: Therefore we speculate that unactivated parenchymal cells offer invasive bacteria a window of opportunity for replication and further dissemination.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation stated in the discussion.

claim: Some pathogens have evolved mechanisms to suppress Perforin-2.
source: A second issue is that some pathogens have evolved mechanisms to suppress Perforin-2 (see accompanying report by McCormack et al.).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and refers to an accompanying manuscript.

claim: When Perforin-2 is expressed at optimal levels, highly pathogenic and antibiotic-resistant bacteria can be killed by Perforin-2.
source: On the other hand, our data also shows that when Perforin-2 is expressed at optimal levels, highly pathogenic and antibiotic-resistant bacteria can be killed by Perforin-2.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Supraphysiologic levels of Perforin-2 expression could be an approach to defeat antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
source: This leads us to speculate that supraphysiologic levels of Perforin-2 expression could be an approach to defeat antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation stated in the discussion.

claim: Serious clinically relevant infections including antibiotic resistant strains of MRSA, S. typhimurium, and M. avium as well as M. tuberculosis are all susceptible to Perforin-2.
source: Vice versa, serious clinically relevant infections including antibiotic resistant strains of MRSA (Figure 7), S. typhimurium (Figure 8), and M. avium as well as M. tuberculosis (Figure 1) are all susceptible to Perforin-2, as demonstrated by greater bacterial pathogenesis in the absence of Perforin-2.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figures 1, 7, and 8.

claim: The antibacterial properties of Perforin-2 involve polymerization and pore-formation in bacteria.
source: These results strongly imply that the antibacterial properties of Perforin-2 involve polymerization and pore-formation in bacteria.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Perforin-2 could be cleaved physiologically at some point during the bacterial infection.
source: The detection of cleavage proteins suggests that Perforin-2 also could be cleaved physiologically at some point during the bacterial infection; however, the order of cleavage and pore-formation as well as the role of additional proteins requires further investigation.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation stated in the discussion.

claim: MAC-polyC9 pores act as entry point for serum lysozyme to digest peptidoglycan resulting in bacterial collapse and lysis.
source: MAC-polyC9 pores act as entry point for serum lysozyme to digest peptidoglycan resulting in bacterial collapse and lysis (Schreiber et al., 1979).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Poly-Perforin-1 pores provide access to multiple granzymes that promote apoptosis of virally infected cells.
source: Poly-Perforin-1 pores provide access to multiple granzymes that promote apoptosis of virally infected cells (Dennert and Podack, 1983; Podack and Konigsberg, 1984; Masson and Tschopp, 1987; Jenne and Tschopp, 1988; Trapani et al., 1988; Shiver et al., 1992; Smyth et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Poly-Perforin-2 pores enhance the delivery and action of endogenously produced ROS and RNS.
source: Likewise, our studies suggest that poly-Perforin-2 pores enhance the delivery and action of endogenously produced ROS and RNS.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: Physiological endogenous levels of lysozyme, ROS, or RNS may be limiting, requiring assistance by poly-Perforin-2 pore-formation to achieve bacterial killing.
source: Although high levels of lysozyme, ROS, or RNS can kill pathogens in the absence of Perforin-2 in vitro, we suggest that physiological endogenous levels of these–and potentially other antimicrobial effectors–may be limiting, requiring assistance by poly-Perforin-2 pore-formation to achieve bacterial killing (see Figure 3 and its supplements).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation stated in the discussion.

claim: The pathogenicity of bacteria may depend on their ability to subvert or evade Perforin-2′s pore-forming ability.
source: Given the central role of Perforin-2 in antimicrobial responses, the pathogenicity of bacteria may depend on their ability to subvert or evade Perforin-2′s pore-forming ability.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation stated in the discussion.

claim: One bacterial virulence factor (Cif) protects bacterial pathogens by blocking translocation of Perforin-2.
source: In the accompanying manuscript we describe one such virulence factor (Cif) that protects bacterial pathogens by blocking translocation of Perforin-2 (McCormack et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and refers to an accompanying manuscript.

claim: Determining the mechanism of how other pathogenic bacteria inhibit Perforin-2 will elucidate additional critical steps in Perforin-2 activation.
source: Determining the mechanism of how other pathogenic bacteria inhibit Perforin-2 will elucidate additional critical steps in Perforin-2 activation and may allow the development of new treatments targeting both antibiotic-sensitive and antibiotic-resistant bacterial pathogens.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation stated in the discussion.

claim: Understanding how pathogenic bacteria inhibit Perforin-2 may allow the development of new treatments targeting both antibiotic-sensitive and antibiotic-resistant bacterial pathogens.
source: Determining the mechanism of how other pathogenic bacteria inhibit Perforin-2 will elucidate additional critical steps in Perforin-2 activation and may allow the development of new treatments targeting both antibiotic-sensitive and antibiotic-resistant bacterial pathogens.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation stated in the discussion.
